image_description: A close-up, eye-level shot of a Nile crocodile partially submerged in murky water. The image focuses on the head and upper dorsal ridge, showing textured, armored skin (scutes) breaking the water surface. Water droplets are visible splashing near the snout. The background is a soft-focus brown/green, suggesting a riverbank or muddy water environment.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is broad and triangular with a V-shaped snout (narrower than alligator).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible portion of the snout shows the characteristic tapering V-shape of a crocodilian, distinct from the U-shape of an alligator. The head structure appears robust and triangular.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Jaws are massive with numerous conical, interlocking teeth visible when mouth is closed.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The mouth is closed and the jawline is largely submerged or obscured by the angle and water line. Individual teeth are not clearly distinguishable in this specific view.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Eyes are positioned dorsally on the head with vertical slit pupils and a nictitating membrane.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The eye is clearly visible on the top of the head (dorsal position). The pupil appears as a vertical slit. The nictitating membrane is not clearly deployed but the eye structure is anatomically correct for a crocodile.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Nostrils are positioned at the tip of the snout.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The nostrils are visible at the anterior end of the snout, positioned high enough to remain above water while the rest of the head is submerged.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is elongated and heavily armored.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible dorsal ridge shows heavy armor plating (scutes). While the full length isn't visible, the continuity of the armored back implies an elongated body typical of the species.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is covered in thick, bony scutes (osteoderms) arranged in regular longitudinal rows along the dorsal surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The texture of the skin above the water line clearly displays rough, raised, bony scutes arranged in a pattern consistent with crocodilian anatomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Scutes are dark brown to grey with a rough, heavily textured appearance.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The coloration is a mix of earthy browns and greys, and the texture is visibly rough and granular, matching the description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Ventral surface is covered in smooth, rectangular scales that are pale yellow to white.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The ventral (belly) side is completely submerged and not visible in this image.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Limbs are short and stout with webbed feet; forelimbs have five digits, hind limbs have four.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: No limbs are visible in the frame; the subject is submerged up to the neck/shoulders.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is laterally compressed and muscular, comprising half of total body length.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is outside the field of view.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The water ripples immediately surrounding the snout appear slightly 'smudged' or painterly rather than having crisp fluid dynamics. The transition between the solid scutes and the liquid water lacks some physical precision, though it is subtle.

artifact_observations.location: Background and far-right edge of the subject
artifact_observations.reasoning: Standard depth-of-field blur is present, but the fall-off on the right side of the crocodile's head feels slightly abrupt, potentially indicating a minor segmentation or focus map artifact common in AI generation.
